title: Describing ends and tangles (and their edge variants) through Boolean algebras and functors
summary: The end space of an infinite graph arises naturally in many contexts as an important invariant and an interesting construction. It compactifies a locally finite graph and Diestel shows how to extend the end space to a larger space, called the tangle space, which is able to compactify any infinite graph. In both ends and tangles, it is the vertex-connectivity structure of the graph that is being studied. If we switch our attention to edge-connectivity, we can analogously define edge-ends.
